purpose: Prespecified design for the supplement measurements. Written before any of the runs named here existed: no run F-J query file, no text-only run B/C answer, no raw-index or dense-tool answer, no shuffled-anchor output and no second Codex re-derivation answer was present when this file was written.

scoring.primary: exact row-set match of score_chain_eval.py (recorded meeting notation)
scoring.secondary: same_meeting rule of score_meeting_spelling_sensitivity.py, reported next to the primary count for every method
scoring.note: The records hold RAN1#100 and RAN1#100-e as two meetings, so the recorded rule stays primary.

queryWriters.sessions: one fresh context-free Claude Opus 5.5 subagent per working group, language and run (50 new sessions; 10 sessions per working group and language with runs A-E)
queryWriters.prompt: the archived run A-E prompt of the same working group and language with only the run letter in the output file name and the scratch folder changed
queryWriters.execution: execute_repeated_runs.sh, first query only, no repair rounds for the primary metric
queryWriters.aggregate: mean exact count over the ten runs A-J; 95% percentile cluster bootstrap over the 35 (wg, family) clusters, 10,000 resamples, seed 20261112; a second interval also resamples the ten runs
queryWriters.rule: The number of runs (ten) is fixed here and is not changed after scores are seen. A session that ends without a complete query file is relaunched once with the same prompt as a fresh session and the relaunch is recorded.

textOnlySearch.sessions: 15 fresh subagents per run with the packets, tool and task text of run A (45 sessions with run A)
textOnlySearch.aggregate: mean over three runs with the same cluster bootstrap

rawIndexSearch.sessions: 15 fresh Claude Opus 5.5 subagents per run, the 15 parts of the text-search packets (same items and order)
rawIndexSearch.tool: search_raw_text.py: BM25 / FTS5 search over the source text of the working-group chunks (record-built label lines removed) and of the TSG plenary documents; a result shows only the file-name document number or the plenary file names and its text; no record-built metadata is searched or shown
rawIndexSearch.recorded: tool runs per item, wall-clock per session, answers
rawIndexSearch.aggregate: mean over two runs with the same cluster bootstrap

denseToolSearch.sessions: 15 fresh Claude Opus 5.5 subagents per run, same parts
denseToolSearch.tool: search_records_dense.py: the agent writes its own queries; each query is embedded with the local bge-m3 encoder and the nearest chunks of the three working-group collections are printed with the same metadata line and text as the text-search tool; there is no exact identifier filter and no keyword expression
denseToolSearch.aggregate: mean over two runs with the same cluster bootstrap

accessByReaderGrid.note: The agent rows are tool-using sessions and the local-reader rows are single prompts over a fixed context; the grid is reported with that condition stated.

shuffledAnchorControl.rule: Within each (wg, family) cell with at least two items, items are ordered by SHA-256 of 'shuffled-anchor:<item id>' and each item receives the question (hence the anchors) of the next item in that order (cyclic shift by one), keeping its own gold. Raw identifier-following containment (measure_raw_source_route.py, same variants) is then counted against the item's own gold. Cells with one item are left out and counted.
shuffledAnchorControl.reported: allRows containment per variant under shuffled anchors next to the matched-anchor counts, and the context sizes

differentFamilyRederivation.solver: Codex CLI (gpt-6.1-sol), same instructions, record files and work-folder isolation as the first held-out Codex round
differentFamilyRederivation.sample: every admitted item that no earlier re-derivation round held (build_fresh_rederivation_packets.py with both earlier folders as --previous, seed 'second-codex-rederivation', per-cell large enough to take all remaining items)
differentFamilyRederivation.scoring: score_fresh_rederivation.py; disagreements are checked against the records and reported one by one

notAnalysed: No run is dropped after its score is seen. Conditions that cannot be completed are reported as incomplete with the reason.
